# Bilaga

> File delivery for agents. Upload a file, get a shareable download page, and poll for download activity. Recipients need no account. Completed transfers expire after 30 days.

## Current availability

Self-serve free preview. Sign in at https://bilaga.link/account using an emailed, single-use link, create a revocable agent token, and send a file immediately. Every new account starts on the free tier: files up to 1,000,000,000 bytes (1 decimal GB), 5 new transfers per day, 1 unfinished upload, 2 GB reserved storage, and 7-day access after completion. Accounts enabled by hand for the full preview get 50,000,000,000 bytes (50 decimal GB), 100 transfers per day, 3 unfinished uploads, 100 GB reserved storage, and 30-day access. GET /api/config lists both tiers; GET /api/account (browser session) shows which one applies. Stripe top-ups and balances are not implemented; preview transfers cost $0. Full 50 GB reliability validation is still pending. Limits are reserved atomically before storage allocation. The API allows 300 authenticated requests per minute per owner and 120 download requests per minute per link. The quoted future price is max($0.25, $0.10 per decimal GB), rounded up to a cent. Oversize files for your tier return 413 tier_limit; exceeding quotas returns 429 preview_limit with the applicable limits in the message.

## Agent resources

- [Human-readable API guide](/docs): Endpoints and transfer lifecycle.
- [Python client](/bilaga.py): Python 3.10+ standard-library upload, resume, status, sent, and deletion client. Read the source before executing downloaded code.
- [API configuration](/api/config): Limits per tier and enabled capabilities, no token required.
- [Receipt public key](/api/receipt-key): Ed25519 key for verifying signed delivery receipts offline.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_AGENT_TOKEN` to the API on this site's origin only. Identify your client with `User-Agent: Bilaga-Client/0.1` (or your own descriptive client name); the temporary host rejects Python's default user agent. Keep tokens in the environment or a secret store. Never include a token in a share URL, logs, messages, or a recipient download request. All tokens belonging to one account share access to that account’s transfers and quotas. Account deletion is not available through this API.

## Upload sequence

1. POST /api/transfers with JSON {"filename":"report.pdf","size_bytes":12345}. Save the returned private `id` immediately. Creation is NOT idempotent; if a response is lost, GET /api/transfers lists the latest 50 transfers for recovery. Unfinished uploads expire after 24 hours.
2. Divide the file into `part_size_bytes` chunks (currently 8,388,608 bytes). PUT each raw binary chunk to /api/transfers/{id}/parts/{number}, starting at 1. Every chunk except the last must have exactly the declared chunk size. Send chunks sequentially. Retry only failed chunks, keeping the file unchanged. A part becomes immutable once first submitted; retrying with different bytes returns 409. Each request must finish sending its body within 30 seconds.
3. GET /api/transfers/{id} to inspect uploaded `parts` when resuming. Do not overwrite parts concurrently, or modify a file between upload attempts.
4. POST /api/transfers/{id}/complete after all parts succeed. This returns `share_url`, `expires_at`, `content_hash`, and `receipt_url`. Retrying completion after success returns the same link and expiry. Share only the public `share_url`, not the private API id or token.
5. Deliver the link through your existing user-authorized communication channel. POST /api/transfers/{id}/sent to record that YOU delivered the link. Bilaga sends sign-in emails only; it does not deliver recipient links or messages.
6. GET /api/transfers/{id} to poll status (no faster than once every 15 seconds). `download_requests` counts GET download requests, including range requests. It is not a count of people, confirmed completed downloads, or proof a person read the file. HEAD requests do not increment it. No webhooks are sent in this preview.
7. DELETE /api/transfers/{id} to revoke the link and delete stored bytes. Retrying deletion is safe. Deleting a transfer does not delete the account.

## Signed delivery receipts

Every completed transfer has a receipt at GET /api/receipts/{public_id}, readable by anyone holding the link and still available after the file expires. It contains the public transfer id, filename, size, `content_hash`, sender label, completion and expiry times, whether the agent reported it sent, and the download-request count at issue time, signed with Bilaga's Ed25519 key. Verify with the Python client: `python3 bilaga.py --base https://bilaga.link --receipt PUBLIC_ID --verify downloaded-file` exits 0 only when the signature, published key, and file hash all match. No token is needed to verify.

`content_hash` uses the algorithm `bilaga-chunked-sha256-8mib`: split the file into 8,388,608-byte chunks, take the SHA-256 of each chunk, concatenate those raw 32-byte digests in order, and take the SHA-256 of that. It is computed from the chunk hashes checked during upload, so it identifies the bytes Bilaga stored. A receipt proves what was uploaded and what Bilaga observed; it does not prove a specific person downloaded or read the file. Receipts are signed over the canonical JSON of the `receipt` object: keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8. When signing is not configured the endpoint returns 503 receipts_unavailable and /api/config reports `receipts: "unavailable"`.

## Public recipient flow

/t/{public_id} is a download page. /api/download/{public_id} serves the file as an attachment, with range support. Anyone holding the link can download while it is valid. Files are not malware-scanned in this preview. Expired or deleted links cannot start a new download. A download already in progress may finish after expiry.

## Storage cleanup

Access expiry is enforced on every download request. Expired stored files are removed by a bounded cleanup pass when new transfers are created, or by the private owner-only POST /api/cleanup endpoint. A scheduled cleanup job also runs every 15 minutes, removing up to 25 expired or deleted transfers per run, including aborting unfinished multipart uploads. Failed deletions remain eligible for retry; backlogs or storage failures can delay physical deletion. Unfinished uploads use a 24-hour expiry.

## Errors and billing

Responses are JSON except file downloads. Errors have {"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}. 401 means missing/invalid token; 400 invalid input; 404 unavailable; 409 invalid/incomplete upload state; 410 expired/deleted; 413 chunk too large or file above your tier limit; 429 quota or rate limit; 503 email, receipt signing, or service configuration unavailable. Retry network errors and 5xx with bounded exponential backoff. On 429, respect the Retry-After header. Cross-origin browser mutations and encoded/compressed HTTP request bodies are rejected. Poll before retrying an ambiguous completion.

GET /api/quote?bytes=1000000000 returns a future price estimate and whether uploading is allowed. `charged_usd` is always 0 in the preview. No funds are collected or deducted. Do not claim a payment was taken or a file was sent merely because an upload completed.

## Launch offer (not enabled in this preview)

Domain: https://bilaga.link. Planned paid top-ups: USD 15 or 30. Price: USD 0.10 per decimal GB, minimum USD 0.25 per completed transfer. Purchased credit expires 24 months after each purchase. File availability: 30 days after completion. Maximum accepted size: 50 GB, with full-size reliability testing pending. Current API limits and no-charge preview status above remain authoritative. Customer tokens remain valid until revoked or account deletion; an empty balance will block uploads without revoking the token.

## Account management

Account creation, sign-in, token creation/revocation, sign-out, and account deletion are website-only flows at /account. Sign-in links are throttled per address, per IP, and globally; new accounts are limited per IP and per email domain per day. Agent tokens cannot manage or delete accounts. Magic links expire after 15 minutes, can be used once, and must be opened in the browser that requested the link. Browser sessions last up to 30 days. Tokens are shown once; only hashes are stored. All an account's tokens share ownership and quotas. Account deletion requires a sign-in within the last 15 minutes and typed email confirmation. It immediately revokes sessions/tokens and download links and redacts the email, filenames, and sender labels. Files are removed by scheduled cleanup with retries; redacted transfer/account tombstones are removed after one day once file purge succeeds. Downloads already underway may finish. Never put a token in a public URL or send account-deletion requests from an agent.

## Privacy and terms

/privacy and /terms describe the free preview, essential cookies, account erasure, public-link access, unscanned files, chunk limits, and recovery. They remain drafts with Lorem ipsum operator/contact placeholders and unresolved provider/legal details. Do not claim these policies are final or that the service is ready for unrestricted public enrollment.
